'''Alan David Weinstein''' (born 17 June 1943) is a professor of [[mathematics]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], working in the field of [[differential geometry]], and especially in [[Poisson manifold|Poisson geometry]].

== Early life and education ==
Weinstein was born in New York City.<ref>''American Men and Women of Science'', Thomson Gale, 2005</ref>  After attending [[Roslyn High School]],<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Bursztyn |first1=Henrique |last2=Fernandes |first2=Rui Loja |author-link2=Rui Loja Fernandes |date=2023-01-01 |title=A Conversation with Alan Weinstein |journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=70 |issue=1 |pages=1 |doi=10.1090/noti2595 |s2cid=254776861 |issn=0002-9920|doi-access=free }}</ref> Weinstein obtained a bachelor's degree at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1964. His teachers included, among others, [[James Munkres]], [[Gian-Carlo Rota]], [[Irving Segal]], and, for the first senior course of differential geometry, [[Sigurður Helgason (mathematician)|Sigurður Helgason]].<ref name=":1" /> He received a PhD at [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1967 under the direction of [[Shiing-Shen Chern]]. His dissertation was entitled "''The [[Cut locus (Riemannian manifold)|cut locus]] and conjugate locus of a [[Riemannian manifold]]''".<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Alan Weinstein - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=31515|access-date=2021-07-17|website=www.mathgenealogy.org}}</ref>

== Career ==
Weinstein worked then at MIT on 1967 (as [[Moore Instructor|Moore instructor]]) and at [[University of Bonn|Bonn University]] in 1968/69. In 1969 he returned to Berkeley as assistant professor and from 1976 he is full professor. During 1975/76 he visited [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques|IHES]] in Paris<ref name=":1" /> and during 1978/79 he was visiting professor at [[Rice University]]. Weinstein was awarded in 1971 a [[Sloan Research Fellowship]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Past Fellows {{!}} Alfred P. Sloan Foundation|url=https://sloan.org/past-fellows|access-date=2021-07-17|website=sloan.org|language=en|archive-date=2018-03-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180314000756/https://sloan.org/past-fellows|url-status=dead}}</ref> and in [[List of Guggenheim Fellowships awarded in 1985|1985]] a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=John Simon Guggenheim Foundation {{!}} Alan David Weinstein|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/alan-david-weinstein/|access-date=2021-07-17|language=en-US}}</ref> In 1978 he was [[Invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians|invited speaker]] at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Helsinki.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1978.2/ICM1978.2.ocr.pdf|title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematician 1978|year=1980|editor-last=[[Olli Lehto|Lehto]]|editor-first=Olii|volume=2|location=Helsinki|pages=803}}</ref> In [[List of American Academy of Arts and Sciences members (1953–1993)#1992|1992]] he was elected Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Alan David Weinstein|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/alan-david-weinstein|access-date=2021-07-17|website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences|language=en}}</ref> and in 2012 Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |date=August 25, 2018 }}, retrieved 2013-09-01.</ref> In 2003 he was awarded an [[Honorary Doctorate|honorary doctorate]] from [[Universiteit Utrecht]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Archive Honorary Doctorates |url=https://www.uu.nl/en/organisation/about-us/tradition-and-history/awards-and-distinctions/honorary-doctorates/archive-honorary-doctorates |access-date=2023-01-28 |website=[[Universiteit Utrecht]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |date=Fall 2003 |title=Honors and Awards |url=https://math.berkeley.edu/sites/default/files/pages/Fall03.pdf |journal=Berkeley Mathematics Newsletter |volume=X |issue=1 |pages=10}}</ref>

==Research==
Weinstein's works cover many areas in [[differential geometry]] and [[mathematical physics]], including [[Riemannian geometry]], [[symplectic geometry]], [[Lie groupoid]]s, [[geometric mechanics]] and [[deformation quantization]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite book |url=https://media.hugendubel.de/shop/coverscans/889PDF/8897259_lprob_1.pdf |title=The Breadth of Symplectic and Poisson Geometry - Festschrift in Honor of Alan Weinstein |publisher=[[Birkhäuser]] |year=2005 |isbn=978-0-8176-3565-7 |editor-last=Marsden |editor-first=Jerrold |editor-link=Jerrold E. Marsden |pages=ix - xii |language=en |chapter=Preface |series=Progress in Mathematics |volume=232 |doi=10.1007/b138687 |editor-last2=Ratiu |editor-first2=Tudor |editor-link2=Tudor Ratiu}}</ref>

Among his most important contributions, in 1971 he proved a [[Weinstein's tubular neighbourhood theorem|tubular neighbourhood theorem]] for [[Lagrangian submanifold|Lagrangians]] in [[symplectic manifold]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=1971-06-01|title=Symplectic manifolds and their lagrangian submanifolds|journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]]|language=en|volume=6|issue=3|pages=329–346|doi=10.1016/0001-8708(71)90020-X|doi-access=free|issn=0001-8708|last1=Weinstein|first1=Alan}}</ref>

In 1974 he worked with [[Jerrold E. Marsden|Jerrold Marsden]] on the theory of reduction for mechanical systems with [[Symmetry|symmetries]], introducing the famous [[Marsden-Weinstein quotient|Marsden–Weinstein quotient]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Marsden|first1=Jerrold|last2=Weinstein|first2=Alan|date=1974-02-01|title=Reduction of symplectic manifolds with symmetry|url=http://www.cds.caltech.edu/~marsden/bib/1974/01-MaWe1974/|journal=Reports on Mathematical Physics|language=en|volume=5|issue=1|pages=121–130|doi=10.1016/0034-4877(74)90021-4|bibcode=1974RpMP....5..121M |issn=0034-4877}}</ref>

In 1978 he formulated a celebrated [[Weinstein conjecture|conjecture]] on the existence of [[periodic orbit]]s,<ref>{{Cite journal|date=1979-09-01|title=On the hypotheses of Rabinowitz' periodic orbit theorems|journal=Journal of Differential Equations|language=en|volume=33|issue=3|pages=353–358|doi=10.1016/0022-0396(79)90070-6|doi-access=free|issn=0022-0396|last1=Weinstein|first1=Alan|bibcode=1979JDE....33..353W }}</ref> which has been later proved in several particular cases and has led to many new developments in [[Symplectic geometry|symplectic]] and [[contact geometry]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Pasquotto|first=Federica|date=2012-09-01|title=A Short History of the Weinstein Conjecture|url=https://doi.org/10.1365/s13291-012-0051-1|journal=Jahresbericht der Deutschen Mathematiker-Vereinigung|language=en|volume=114|issue=3|pages=119–130|doi=10.1365/s13291-012-0051-1|s2cid=120567013|issn=1869-7135|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In 1981 he formulated a general principle, called ''symplectic creed'', stating that "everything is a Lagrangian submanifold".<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Weinstein |first=Alan |date=July 1981 |title=Symplectic geometry |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/bulletin-of-the-american-mathematical-society-new-series/volume-5/issue-1/Symplectic-geometry/bams/1183548217.full |journal=[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=5 |issue=1 |pages=1–13 |doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-1981-14911-9 |via=[[Project Euclid]]|doi-access=free }}</ref> Such insight has been constantly quoted as the source of inspiration for many results in symplectic geometry.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />

Building on the work of [[André Lichnerowicz]], in a 1983 foundational paper<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Weinstein|first=Alan|date=1983-01-01|title=The local structure of Poisson manifolds|journal=Journal of Differential Geometry|volume=18|issue=3|doi=10.4310/jdg/1214437787|doi-access=free|issn=0022-040X}}</ref> Weinstein proved many results which laid the ground for the development of modern [[Poisson manifold|Poisson geometry]]. A further influential idea in this field was its introduction of [[symplectic groupoid]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Weinstein|first=Alan|date=1987|title=Symplectic groupoids and Poisson manifolds|url=https://www.ams.org/bull/1987-16-01/S0273-0979-1987-15473-5/|journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|language=en|volume=16|issue=1|pages=101–104|doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-1987-15473-5|doi-access=free|issn=0273-0979}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Coste|first1=A.|last2=Dazord|first2=P.|last3=Weinstein|first3=A.|date=1987|title=Groupoïdes symplectiques|url=http://www.numdam.org/item/PDML_1987___2A_1_0/|journal=Publications du Département de mathématiques (Lyon)|language=fr|issue=2A|pages=1–62}}</ref>

He is author of more than 50 research papers in peer-reviewed journals and he has supervised 35 PhD students.<ref name=":0" />
